overview: The Mon Calamari Fleet is the backbone of the Rebel Alliance's naval capability. Comprised of converted civilian vessels — originally designed as luxury liners and exploration craft — these ships were repurposed for war after the Mon Calamari and Quarren liberated their homeworld Dac from Imperial occupation. Under the command of Admiral Gial Ackbar, the fleet provides the Alliance with its only capital ships capable of engaging Imperial Star Destroyers in direct combat.
short_descriptor: The Alliance's naval backbone. Mon Calamari shipyards converted civilian vessels into warships — every ship is unique. Admiral Ackbar commands. The fleet is the Alliance's most irreplaceable asset.

how_they_operate.heading: A CONVERTED FLEET
how_they_operate.text: The fleet is built from converted Mon Calamari civilian vessels — luxury liners, exploration craft, and deep-sea transports — repurposed for war at the shipyards of Dac. Each MC80 star cruiser is unique in internal layout because no two civilian vessels were built to the same specification, which makes Imperial tactical prediction difficult but replacement parts a logistical nightmare.

how_they_operate.heading: COMMAND
how_they_operate.text: Admiral Gial Ackbar commands from his flagship and holds the rank of Alliance Fleet Admiral, with individual Mon Calamari captains exercising significant autonomy in battle.

how_they_operate.heading: COMPOSITION
how_they_operate.text: The fleet deploys MC80 cruisers as the battle line, supported by MC30c frigates and MC40a light cruisers as escorts, with up to 56 starfighters per capital ship including the B-wing heavy assault fighter that Ackbar co-developed with Slayn & Korpil.

how_they_operate.heading: CREWS AND SURVIVAL
how_they_operate.text: Crews are drawn from diverse Alliance species but trained to operate ships originally designed for Mon Calamari physiology. The fleet's survival strategy is mobility — it stays ahead of Imperial pursuit through hyperspace, never holding a static position long enough for the Empire to concentrate forces.

witness_statement.text: Did a refit job on an MC80 in drydock. Pulled a bulkhead panel and found a mosaic behind it — ocean scene, hand-laid tile, must've taken someone months. That ship was a pleasure liner eight months ago. They welded gun mounts over the observation deck and left the chandelier hanging in what's now the fire control room. Every ship in that fleet is like that. A cruise ship that learned to kill.
witness_statement.source: Freelance starship mechanic, contracted for Alliance fleet maintenance

motivations.primary: Defense of Mon Cala and destruction of the Empire
secondary: Maintaining the Alliance's only viable capital ship fleet
Proving that converted civilian vessels and superior tactics can defeat Imperial military might
Protecting the shipyards of Dac that produce the Alliance's most powerful warships
Honoring the Mon Calamari tradition of artistry and excellence even in instruments of war
motivations.notes: The Mon Calamari fight not just for the Rebellion but for their own liberation. Their homeworld was enslaved by the Empire for its shipbuilding resources. The fleet represents both military capability and cultural pride — Mon Calamari ship design reflects their artisan traditions even in warships.

strategic: Provide the Rebel Alliance with capital ship capability sufficient to challenge Imperial fleets
Protect Dac as one of the few openly rebellious worlds and the Alliance's primary shipyard
Develop new warship designs and fighter classes to counter evolving Imperial tactics
Maintain Mon Calamari-Quarren unity against Imperial attempts to divide them
operational: Convert civilian vessels to warships rapidly enough to replace combat losses
Execute fleet engagements that maximize the advantages of Mon Calamari ship design
Train crews from diverse Alliance species to operate ships designed for Mon Calamari physiology
Coordinate hit-and-run fleet operations that keep the Alliance one step ahead of Imperial pursuit

avoided: Pitched battles against superior numbers without tactical advantage — Mon Calamari commanders are bold but not suicidal
Abandoning crew or allied vessels — the Mon Calamari's deep loyalty culture extends to fleet operations
Static defense positions — the fleet stays mobile, always a step ahead of the Empire through hyperspace
methods.notes: The fleet operates through a combination of superior ship design, tactical brilliance (particularly Ackbar's), and the willingness to take bold risks. MC80 cruisers are typically deployed with heavy escorts but bold commanders like Ackbar have been known to drive directly into Imperial Navy formations. The fleet's mobility through hyperspace is its primary survival strategy.

strengths: MC80 star cruisers are among the few Rebel ships capable of engaging Imperial Star Destroyers directly
Mon Calamari ship design features unique, non-standardized construction that makes each vessel unpredictable to Imperial tacticians
Admiral Ackbar's tactical foresight and ability to adapt to changing battlefield conditions
Dedicated shipyard capacity on Dac producing both capital ships and advanced fighters like the B-wing
Deep cultural tradition of engineering excellence — Mon Calamari captains know their ships intimately because their species designed and built them
weaknesses: MC80 cruisers are converted civilian vessels — luxury liners, exploration craft, and deep-sea transports — and conversions are frequently incomplete, with hull welds, weapons mounts, and defensive systems untested under combat stress.

Quarren crew members serve throughout the fleet but carry the political burden of their species' documented history of cooperation with the Imperial occupation of Dac, generating persistent trust deficits with Mon Calamari shipmates.
The fleet's shipyard capacity is concentrated on Dac in the Calamari sector, which lies in Imperial-monitored space and is vulnerable to blockade or direct assault.
No two MC80 cruisers share identical internal layouts or systems configurations, making replacement parts non-interchangeable and requiring vessel-specific engineering knowledge for every repair.

Fleet cohesion depends heavily on Admiral Ackbar's personal reputation and tactical authority, and his absence from individual engagements produces measurable delays in inter-ship coordination and command decisions.

behavior_under_threat.low: Patrol cruisers and frigates handle the threat independently. Standard Alliance protocols apply.
behavior_under_threat.medium: Fleet elements concentrate. MC80 cruisers deploy their fighter wings while maintaining long-range bombardment positions.
behavior_under_threat.high: Full fleet mobilization. Ackbar or senior Mon Calamari commanders take direct control. MC80 cruisers form the battle line with MC30c frigates and MC40a light cruisers as escorts.
behavior_under_threat.critical: The fleet fights with everything it has. MC80 cruisers drive directly into enemy formations. Every fighter launches. The survival of the Alliance fleet — and by extension the Rebellion — is at stake.

chain_of_command: Ship bridge crew and tactical officers
Ship captain (often Mon Calamari nemesis-level commander)
Fleet Admiral Ackbar or sector fleet commander
alert_escalation.notes: Naval communication is rapid through encrypted channels. Mon Calamari captains have significant autonomy in battle but defer to fleet commanders for strategic decisions. Ackbar's flagship serves as the command nexus for major engagements.

tension_patterns: Mon Calamari officers and human Alliance commanders frequently differ on tactical doctrine, particularly regarding acceptable risk thresholds for capital ships, with cultural attitudes toward collective sacrifice amplifying strategic disagreements.

MC80 cruisers converted from civilian vessels within the past standard year routinely enter combat with incomplete weapons integration, untested hull reinforcements, and residual civilian systems that interfere with military operations.

Quarren crew members serve alongside Mon Calamari throughout the fleet, but the Quarren species' documented history of cooperation with the Imperial occupation of Dac produces persistent mutual distrust that affects crew cohesion.

Fleet maintenance and refit operations require access to the shipyards on Dac, which are located in Imperial-monitored space, meaning every docking period increases the probability of Imperial detection of Alliance fleet positions.

Admiral Ackbar's personal authority and tactical reputation serve as the primary unifying force across the fleet's diverse command structure, and engagements conducted without his direct oversight consistently produce slower decision-making and inter-captain coordination failures.

mcguffin_interest.notes: The fleet prioritizes military intelligence data (Imperial fleet movements, patrol schedules), weapons systems, and technology that can enhance their ships or produce new fighter designs. Key personnel — engineers, tacticians, defecting Imperial officers — are highly valued. The Mon Calamari have little interest in contraband or artifacts.

relationship_notes.rebel_alliance: The fleet IS the Alliance's naval arm — Mon Calamari cruisers are the only capital ships capable of challenging the Imperial Navy. Admiral Ackbar serves as both fleet commander and senior Alliance military leader.
relationship_notes.imperial_military: The primary adversary — the Empire enslaved Dac for its shipbuilding resources and the fleet exists specifically to destroy Imperial naval power.
relationship_notes.wookiee_clans: Sympathetic fellow victims of Imperial enslavement — Mon Calamari and Wookiee liberation efforts are morally aligned though operationally separate.
relationship_notes.corporate_sector_authority: Minimal contact — the fleet operates far from CSA territory.

prominent_figures.name: Admiral Gial Ackbar
prominent_figures.role: Alliance Fleet Admiral, fleet supreme commander
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Ackbar is the Alliance's irreplaceable naval asset. He commands the only capital fleet capable of engaging Star Destroyers, and every major fleet engagement depends on his tactical judgment. Losing him would set the Alliance Navy back years.
prominent_figures.wants: To liberate Dac from Imperial occupation and prove that the Mon Calamari fleet can defeat the Imperial Navy in decisive engagement.
prominent_figures.secret: Privately fears that the Alliance political leadership will negotiate a peace that leaves Dac under Imperial control, rendering the fleet's sacrifices meaningless.

behavior.under_pressure: Becomes more focused and decisive. His reputation was built on adapting to changing conditions mid-battle — pressure sharpens rather than degrades his performance.
behavior.when_losing: Executes tactical withdrawals designed to preserve fleet assets for the next engagement. Will not sacrifice ships in hopeless actions.
behavior.loyalty: To Dac and to the Alliance cause in that order. The Alliance is the vehicle for Mon Calamari liberation — if it ceased to serve that purpose, the calculus would change.
behavior.tells: When he begins issuing orders in Mon Calamari rather than Basic, the tactical situation has become serious enough that he is no longer performing for non-Mon Calamari bridge crew.

useful_to_players: Commands the Alliance's entire capital ship fleet — his authorization opens every naval resource
Tactical genius applicable to any military problem, not just fleet engagements
His personal endorsement carries more weight with Alliance command than most senators' votes
hooks: Ackbar is looking for independent operators to scout a system before committing fleet assets — he does not trust the standard intelligence channels on this one
An MC80 went silent during a routine patrol and Ackbar has quietly diverted resources to find it before Imperial intelligence notices the gap

prominent_figures.name: Quarrie
prominent_figures.role: Mon Calamari shipwright and prototype designer
prominent_figures.notes: An old shipwright from Mon Calamari who saw what the Republic was becoming and fled to Shantipole to set up a secret workshop. Offered his services to trusted Rebel contacts. Represents the Mon Calamari tradition of brilliant independent engineering.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Quarrie is a reclusive genius working from a hidden workshop on Shantipole. He builds prototypes that change the war — the B-wing came from his drafting table. Getting to him requires knowing where he is, and he prefers it that way.
prominent_figures.wants: To design and build starfighters that give the Alliance a technological edge over Imperial mass production, working on his own terms without military bureaucracy.
prominent_figures.secret: Has design schematics for fighter concepts beyond the B-wing that he has not shared with anyone because he does not trust Alliance procurement to build them correctly.

behavior.under_pressure: Retreats into his work. Engineering problems are solvable; people problems are not. He will lock himself in his workshop and emerge with a solution.
behavior.when_losing: Destroys his prototypes and schematics rather than let them fall into Imperial hands. The designs live in his head — the physical models are expendable.
behavior.loyalty: To his craft and to the Alliance cause, in roughly equal measure. He left Mon Calamari before the Empire arrived because he saw the Republic rotting from within.
behavior.tells: Becomes animated and verbose when discussing engineering. Becomes monosyllabic when discussing anything else. The shift is immediate and obvious.

useful_to_players: Can modify, repair, or improve almost any starfighter or small craft with improvised materials
His Shantipole workshop contains tools and components unavailable through standard Alliance supply
Knows the engineering weaknesses of both Alliance and Imperial ship designs from studying their construction
hooks: Quarrie sent a parts list to an Alliance contact — half the components are restricted Imperial military hardware. He needs a procurement team that does not ask questions.
A prototype Quarrie was testing disappeared during a Shantipole storm. He insists it crashed. The debris field suggests it landed.

prominent_figures.name: Tendaar Bel
prominent_figures.role: Mon Calamari Engineer in the Rebellion
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Tendaar is Alliance engineering corps — the person who keeps converted pleasure liners fighting like warships. Academically trained, methodical, and deeply embedded in fleet maintenance operations. Not glamorous, entirely essential.
prominent_figures.wants: To apply Mon Calamari academic rigor to Alliance engineering problems and earn the professional recognition that his culture values above all else.
prominent_figures.secret: Has documented systemic flaws in the MC80 conversion process that could cause catastrophic hull failures under sustained bombardment. His reports keep getting deprioritized because there are not enough ships to take offline for repairs.

behavior.under_pressure: Becomes clinical and data-driven. He treats emergencies as engineering problems with quantifiable parameters and optimal solutions.
behavior.when_losing: Documents everything. If a ship is going down, Tendaar is recording what failed and why so the next conversion avoids the same mistake.
behavior.loyalty: To the Mon Calamari tradition of academic excellence and to the Alliance as the best available vehicle for Dac's liberation.
behavior.tells: Hesitates before authorizing a ship for combat duty — if the hesitation is long, he has concerns about the hull integrity that he cannot prove.

useful_to_players: Can assess the structural integrity and combat readiness of any Mon Calamari vessel
His maintenance records contain detailed information about every Alliance capital ship's vulnerabilities and capabilities
Academic connections to Mon Calamari engineering institutions provide access to technical knowledge unavailable elsewhere
hooks: Tendaar flagged an MC80 as unfit for combat and the captain overruled him. He is looking for someone to inspect the ship independently before the next engagement.
A set of pre-war Mon Calamari shipyard blueprints surfaced on the black market. Tendaar wants them authenticated before the Alliance commits funds.

prominent_figures.name: Rask Odai
prominent_figures.role: Mon Calamari criminal entrepreneur (Broken Horn Syndicate)
prominent_figures.notes: An enterprising Mon Calamari who used the legitimate trading company Twin Horns Storage to seize economic control of Lothal. Demonstrates that not all Mon Calamari serve the Rebellion — some pursue independent criminal enterprise.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Rask is a Mon Calamari who chose credits over cause. Runs a legitimate front on Lothal while controlling the local black market through the Broken Horn Syndicate. Useful for procurement. Do not mistake his species for his allegiance.
prominent_figures.wants: To expand the Broken Horn Syndicate's economic control on Lothal and beyond, using Twin Horns Storage as a legitimate front for smuggling and market manipulation.
prominent_figures.secret: Has been approached by both the Alliance and the Empire for supply contracts and is playing both sides, delivering just enough to each to maintain leverage without committing to either.

behavior.under_pressure: Calculates. Every threat is weighed against the cost of compliance versus resistance. He will fold instantly if the math favors it.
behavior.when_losing: Liquidates assets and relocates. He built Twin Horns Storage from nothing once and can do it again somewhere the Empire and Alliance are not looking.
behavior.loyalty: To profit. Species solidarity means nothing to him — he will sell to Trandoshans if the margin is right.
behavior.tells: Offers hospitality when he wants something. The quality of the food correlates directly with the size of the favor he is about to ask.

useful_to_players: Controls Lothal's black market supply chains — can source almost anything for the right price
Twin Horns Storage provides legitimate shipping cover for contraband movement
His network of contacts spans the criminal and legitimate business worlds on multiple Outer Rim planets
hooks: Rask lost a warehouse full of inventory to an Imperial raid that felt targeted — he is paying for information on who tipped off the garrison
Twin Horns Storage posted a job for armed escorts on a run to the Kessel sector. The pay is three times the standard rate. Nobody is asking what the cargo is.

source_material_notes: The Mon Calamari Fleet receives extensive coverage across FFG sourcebooks. AoR Core pp.285-286 provides the MC80 Liberty cruiser profile. Alliance Worlds (Strongholds of Resistance) pp.29-36 gives the most detailed treatment of Dac and its society. Commander Sourcebook pp.6-10, 55-56 covers Ackbar and fleet command extensively. The Diplomat Sourcebook p.63 and Starships and Speeders pp.121, 141 add ship profiles and tactical context. The fleet is the most thoroughly documented military force in the FFG line outside the Imperial military.
